Similar pottery, step by step: one bowl photo

Version 2026-11-07 · the 🏺 Similar pottery page of Glaze Search, driven in a browser through five scenarios with one photo, from simple to complicated. Every screenshot is the real page; every number is the page's own result (a test copy of the app with its own logs).

red frame = where to look in the screenshot (the inside stays see-through) · purple = done by the text branch (vendor/gc2_text_branch) · the colour-match model of test_similarity.zip is not used on this page: the pot search uses the project's first recipe model and the photo models.

What the page does

It compares your object with 12,309 objects cut out of Glazy photos and lists the most similar pots. Each pot gets one similarity per component:

ComponentComparesHow
glaze appearancethe look of the glazeDINOv2 (frozen) on the cut-out → the first recipe model's trained image head → cosine
shapethe outline only0.5 × outline measures + 0.5 × DINOv2 on the black silhouette (no colour)
surface / effectsfinish, transparency, effects, defectsthe attribute model's probabilities, Hellinger affinity
colour regionsevery colour area and where it isCIEDE2000 between matched regions + a position penalty
text (optional)your wordscleaned into the training format → the first recipe model's text embedding → cosine
formula (optional)your oxidesthe first recipe model's formula embedding → cosine

How a pot's score is made

z = (similarity − average over all 12,309 pots) ÷ spread   ·   score = Σ share × z

z says how far above an ordinary pot this one is, for that component and this search. The shares: the photo part gets 0.40, split by the preset (Balanced: appearance 0.30 · shape 0.20 · surface 0.15 · colour 0.35); words add 0.35 and a formula 0.25; all are divided by their total so they add up to 1. So the score is not 0–1: 0 is an average pot, 2 means about two spreads above average. The card's Why this rank? shows the similarity per component and the share × z (the "contribution"); the average and spread are not on the page: they are recovered below from the page's own numbers.

Colour regions in detail: for a query region i and a pot region j, cost = min(1, ΔE00 / 40) + 0.5 × (distance between the region centres). Each query region takes its cheapest pot region and each pot region its cheapest query region, weighted by importance (distinctiveness + area + contrast); similarity = 1 − (the two averages) / 2.

Scenario 1 · Only a colour (no photo)

  1. Open 🏺 Similar pottery with no photo.
  2. Card 4 · Colours: type the HEX #0E1F3E (navy) and press Add; "typed / picked" is selected.
  3. Press Search.

Scenario 2 · The photo, Balanced preset (the default)

  1. 📷 My photo: upload the photo. The app cuts out 1 object (the whole bowl).
  2. Press 🏺 Find similar pottery: the page opens and searches at once with the Balanced preset.

  • MIDDLE OF THE NIGHT · 2.26
  • S7 C A3 floating blue · 2.20
  • Midnight Blue · 2.08

nDCG@10 0.80 · Precision@10: shape 0 % · glaze 100 % · colour 100 % · strict 0 %

What it shows: #1 wins mainly on colour (similarity 0.92: nearly the same navy) and glaze look; all ten are glossy and in the colour.

Read the evaluation with care. It never changes the order; it checks each result with rules: shape = the same object form as your object, glaze = the same surface group, colour = within ΔE00 20 of your most important colour region, strict = all three. Here the form guess "plate" is wrong, so "shape ✗" and "strict 0 %" say more about the guess than about the results. Correct the form in card 1b (Your object up close) on 📷 My photo before searching to make those rows meaningful.

Shape now has the largest share, so outlines decide and colour hardly counts (#1 is green, ΔE 24 from the bowl). #1 is a test tile: the bowl fills almost the whole photo, so its outline is close to a full frame, like a tile photographed close up (shape similarity 0.80). #2 and #3 are bowls seen from above, the way this photo was taken. Shape compares the outline in the photo, not the real 3-D form.

Scenario 4 · Photo + words

  1. Card 2 · Words about the pot: firing cone 6, surface Glossy, atmosphere Oxidation.
  2. Press Search (Balanced).

The words are cleaned into the training format by the text branch: Surface: glossy. Firing cone: 6. Atmosphere: oxidation.. The text component joins with share 0.35 next to 0.40 for the photo:

Why words make a photo search worse. Thousands of recipes carry exactly "glossy, cone 6, oxidation", so they all get the same very high text similarity (0.978, z ≈ 5.7). With 47 % of the score, the words then decide the order and push the photo's evidence aside: nDCG@10 falls from 0.80 (scenario 2) to 0.68, and colour precision from 100 % to 60 %. With a photo, leave the words empty; use them when you have no photo.

Scenario 5 · Photo + words + formula

  1. Keep the words of scenario 4.
  2. Card 3 · Formula: paste the formula of a navy glossy glaze (Storm Blue, Glazy #577829, from the recipe catalog) and press Fill: 11 oxides including fluxes, so it is used.
  3. Press Search.

Shares: shape 0.08 · glaze appearance 0.12 · surface / effects 0.06 · colour regions 0.14 · text 0.35 · formula 0.25 (photo 0.40 + words 0.35 + formula 0.25 = 1).

  • A photo alone works best here; the Colour preset gives the best evaluation for a pot that is mostly one strong colour, Shape finds the same form, Glaze / surface finds the same glaze look (check the colours).
  • Words with a photo make the order worse, because thousands of recipes share the same tags; a formula softens that a little.
  • The score is a sum of shares × z: 0 is an average pot. The card's Why this rank? shows each part.
  • The evaluation is only as good as the object's form and surface: correct them in card 1b before trusting "shape" and "strict".
